subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Inflation: The Universe's Growth Spurt
description: A fast breakdown of Inflation: The Universe's Growth Spurt for builders.

hook.text: In a tiny fraction of a second after the Big Bang, the universe expanded faster than the speed of light.

buildup.text: This era of cosmic inflation lasted about a trillionth of a trillionth of a trillionth of a second.

discovery.text: Alan Guth proposed inflation in 1980 to explain why the universe looks the same in every direction.

twist.text: Without inflation, opposite sides of the sky would have never been in contact—yet they share the same temperature.

climax.text: Inflation stretched tiny quantum fluctuations into the seeds of galaxies. Randomness became cosmic structure.

punchline.text: A burst faster than light. It shaped every galaxy we see.

quiz.question: What problem did cosmic inflation solve?
options: Why the universe looks the same temperature in every direction
Why the Big Bang happened at all
Why galaxies are moving apart from each other

details.summary: Cosmic inflation proposes that the universe underwent an exponential expansion in the first tiny fraction of a second — expanding faster than light and doubling in size at least 60 times.
details.whyItMatters: Inflation solves several puzzles of standard Big Bang cosmology — horizon, flatness, and magnetic monopole problems. It also explains the origin of large-scale structure from quantum fluctuations stretched to cosmic scales.
takeaways: The universe expanded exponentially in its first fraction of a second
Inflation explains the universe's remarkable uniformity
Quantum fluctuations during inflation seeded galaxy formation

faq.question: How fast did the universe expand during inflation?
faq.answer: The observable universe may have expanded from smaller than a proton to larger than a grapefruit in roughly 10⁻³² seconds. This is far faster than light — which doesn't violate relativity because it's space itself expanding, not objects moving through space.

faq.question: Has inflation been proven?
faq.answer: Inflation makes predictions that match observations (flatness, uniformity, structure patterns). However, the specific mechanism driving inflation remains debated.
